channel.description: Recent content in Weekly Summaries on TzJ's Net

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W29
item.description: This week marked a critical inflection point for the GR00T VLA project, transitioning from experimental setup to validated deployment configurations. The most significant achievement was identifying and correcting infrastructure artifacts that produced false ‘100% success’ metrics, leading to the establishment of W8A8 as the optimal quantization schema (98.5% accuracy, 410ms latency reduction). Concurrently, the ErrorRecoveryBenchmark data strategy was rigorously defined and sanitized, revealing a severe scarcity of qualified human demos (<2% yield) which necessitates new collection strategies. On the software engineering front, significant storage hygiene was achieved on Tianhe3 HPC, cross-repo bugs were resolved, and desktop tools (LiveCaption, TokenMonitor) were stabilized across Windows/macOS environments.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W28
item.description: This week marked significant milestones across multiple core projects, most notably the completion of the Idea-to-Plane Pipeline MVP for LifeCopilot and TokenMonitor v0.14.1 release. Critical infrastructure challenges on restricted HPC clusters were resolved through custom dependency shimming and proxy tunneling. Concurrently, MeetingHelper achieved robust local dual-source audio transcription by bypassing OS-specific API limitations, while extensive robotic model evaluation provided actionable failure data for Action-Sketcher and broader robotics frameworks.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W26
item.description: This week, key infrastructure optimization and research validation were achieved in the fields of artificial intelligence tools, spatial transcriptomics, and robot simulation. The AI Companion dual-agent ecosystem addresses cross-platform hook equity and concurrency issues, making skill deployment smoother. A robot evaluation process was successfully established on Tianhe-2, which confirmed the limitations of zero-sample VLM and verified the need for a world model for time context. Spatial omics analysis resolved the “FM paradox” and negated the feasibility of JEPA, prompting a shift toward candidate selection strategies. Infrastructure improvements include automated server access scripts, encrypted Live DAG visualization features, and strict audit verification mechanisms to eliminate artificial intelligence hallucination fluctuations.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W25
item.description: This week, significant cross-functional progress was made in the fields of spatial genomics, robot evaluation, desktop application development, and AI workflow infrastructure. Key achievements include: migrating MIHD clustering to the Leiden platform and conducting comprehensive ablation studies; validating the baseline models of NVIDIA Predict 2.5 and RoboCasa recovery; enhancing the single-instance execution and device synchronization mechanism of TokenMonitor; and optimizing the macOS interface lifecycle and performance of Desktop Video. Additionally, a portable Repository-to-DAG document workflow was established, addressing critical data source and benchmark infrastructure issues, and the AI provider configuration was migrated to the AWS Claude platform, laying a solid foundation for experimental validation and software release.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W24
item.description: This week marked a significant shift from protocol realignment to execution across benchmarking, robotics research, and application engineering. The Error Recovery Benchmark successfully corrected critical spec misalignments by anchoring evaluation metrics to the authoritative M16/Panorama framework, enabling statistically valid deployment on Tianhe2. Concurrently, the Gadget ecosystem underwent a comprehensive architectural migration to ccusage 20.x alongside the remediation of 58 bugs, primarily targeting cache poisoning and exception handling leaks. Application development progressed through high-impact optimizations in TokenMonitor (CPU hotspot resolution) and Desktop Video (Apple-compliant UI redesign), while infrastructure diagnostics cleared hardware false positives and Secure Boot driver conflicts. AI strategy work synthesized actionable JEPA directions and rigorously validated UNI2’s superiority over stochastic baselines via extensive statistical sweeps.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W23
item.description: This week, intensive infrastructure modernization efforts, critical data recovery work, and comprehensive project implementations for multiple code repositories were carried out. Key achievements include: migrating AI tools to AWS through strict permission controls; restoring missing spatial transcriptome research data that was missing for several months using NetApp snapshots; stabilizing the CI/CD process for AI Dev Companion; and enhancing the deployment process for the TokenMonitor branch. Meanwhile, the Gadget project also completed its comprehensive implementation, along with a restructuring plan based on risk levels. In the latter part of the week, focus was placed on the rigorous validation methods for the Error Recovery Benchmark, successfully replacing vague documentation with a structured test-priority framework, and verifying through resistance tests.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W22
item.description: This week centered on stabilizing, securing, and re-architecting the AI-assisted development environment across multiple interconnected projects. Major accomplishments include successfully migrating the Claude Code backend from AWS Bedrock to the Claude Platform on AWS, engineering a deterministic DAG-based task execution engine (ccedit), and eliminating critical runtime stability issues in LifeCopilot and TokenMonitor. Extensive configuration standardization was achieved through lifecycle scripts and centralized startup orchestrators across nine repositories, while parallel efforts resolved complex Windows shell encoding conflicts and persistent disk/memory cache inconsistencies. Infrastructure debt was systematically addressed, cost visibility risks were mitigated, and professional portfolio materials were modernized, setting a robust foundation for scalable AI-driven workflows next week.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W21
item.description: This week centered on two parallel workstreams: auditing the TokenMonitor agentic workflow protocol and executing strategic research for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. Significant progress was made in identifying critical documentation-to-runtime gaps, resolving Python import isolation issues, and synthesizing cutting-edge VLA paper findings into three actionable research directions. Development momentum was temporarily halted due to enterprise policy restrictions on AI tooling, while deep architectural insights around spatial memory, hypernetwork-based decoupling, and extreme edge quantization were established.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W20
item.description: Over the past week, development efforts mainly focused on establishing a unified proxy-based workflow system, migrating the core development environment to optimize storage space, and resolving key deployment bottlenecks in the Summarize project. The team successfully designed and deployed a standardized “spec-to-review” protocol across three repositories. After migrating the Conda/Pip infrastructure, over 70 GB of disk space was freed up, and the pipeline configuration issues that caused the report deployment to be blocked for 72 days were fixed. Although much of the infrastructure and tool-related work was completed in early this week, development efforts were briefly paused during the middle of the week before resuming through the optimization of the CLI standardization and basic data reconstruction functions.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W19
item.description: This week centered on the final release and architectural stabilization of TokenMonitor v0.13.1 alongside extensive preparation for the ErrorRecoveryBench/RecoverBench NeurIPS 2026 submission, including comprehensive code anonymization, dataset validation, metric correction, and Croissant metadata generation. Parallel computational efforts resolved persistent hardware stability issues by diagnosing and patching an RTX 5090 PCIe driver crash loop, while simultaneously repairing corrupted LeRobot dataset pipelines with robust JAX-compatible error handling and auditing the AdaptVision PPO training architecture. The week concluded with a successfully merged codebase, verified academic submission materials, restored workstation reliability, and optimized local development infrastructure.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W18
item.description: This week focused on stabilizing and releasing the TokenMonitor desktop application (v0.12.1 → v0.12.3) through key Windows UI/UX fixes, the Cursor IDE automatic reconnection feature, and strict CI/CD execution mechanisms. Meanwhile, the development of the robot ML pipeline was advanced via targeted telemetry data collection, remote transmission verification, and comprehensive model benchmarking; some issues in the v2 versions required architectural investigations. Additionally, the Gadget reports from the past two months have been compiled and uploaded to GitHub Pages for release. This week also highlighted the importance of multi-level debugging in ML development for solving platform-specific problems, as well as the necessity of strict pre-release verification processes and task-aware evaluation strategies. It also underscored ongoing dependencies regarding automated environment configuration and cross-device authentication.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W17
item.description: This week centered on architectural modernization, cost optimization, and pipeline stabilization across core infrastructure and feature development. Key achievements include completing a comprehensive audit and modular delivery of the LifeCopilot Idea Pipeline, migrating voice transcription to local Whisper backends, and resolving critical build pipeline issues that restored bilingual chart consistency. Concurrently, extensive token usage analytics were generated, revealing cache dominance in LLM consumption, while system maintenance covered dual-boot GRUB configuration and early-stage Tauri v0.11.1 integration efforts despite branch divergence challenges.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W16
item.description: This week delivered a comprehensive consolidation of research breakthroughs and cross-platform infrastructure hardening, culminating in a publication-ready NeurIPS manuscript for spatial transcriptomics, advanced architectural formulations for a battery degradation foundation model, and modernized robotics simulation pipelines. Key achievements include resolving critical computational bottlenecks (O(n²) conversion scaling, latent norm collapse, and GPU version mismatches), eliminating silent data corruption in bilingual translation workflows via explicit validation gates, and streamlining AI infrastructure billing with dynamic version parsing. The week successfully bridged theoretical ML development with production-grade toolchain stability, establishing robust baselines for empirical training, automated deployment pipelines, and deterministic cross-device synchronization ahead of upcoming submission and scaling cycles.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W15
item.description: This week, comprehensive progress was made in the fields of robot benchmark validation, terminal simulation architectures, and spatial transcriptomics. Key silent process failures were successfully resolved, and standardization of cross-platform infrastructure was achieved. Important milestones include solving the deterministic replay and tensor alignment issues in the MimicGen/RobotBench process, shifting the focus of MIHD papers toward trade-off analysis for zero-sample foundation model fusion, releasing the BetterSSH v0.1.0 version with universal terminal routing capabilities, and stabilizing the TokenMonitor pricing cache and Gadget repository synchronization function. Environment tests that are platform-independent, clear verifier state management, and constraint-based planning strategies help enhance the stability of the CI workflow, ensure strict metadata contracts, and provide a solid foundation for subsequent VLA integration and NeurIPS transfer processes.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W14
item.description: This week focuses on stabilizing the key infrastructure in cross-platform desktop deployment, space genomics benchmark tests, and robot simulation validation, while advancing the writing of academic manuscripts. Key achievements include resolving serious bill duplication issues, silent CI/CD execution failures, pipeline cache corruption problems, and complex Linux Wayland/GTK compositor performance issues. Important milestones include the release of v0.6.1 TokenMonitor client with a fixed-size UI architecture, the integration of MIHD space genomics benchmark data, the generation of a reliable M12/M13 evaluation dataset with dynamic motion tracking, the development of a production-standard dual-language Hugo middleware, the refactoring of Life-Copilot into a multi-CLI orchestration framework, and the stabilization of Crossformer battery training metrics. The current progress direction is to complete benchmark evaluation, manuscript visualization, and fine-tuning of the VLA model, thereby bringing the related base code library into a production-ready state.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W13
item.description: This week, focus was placed on large-scale architecture decomposition, stability optimization for cross-platform desktop applications, and the integration of benchmark testing processes. Key achievements include modularizing the Gadget integrated research toolkit, successfully migrating the TokenMonitor desktop application to a fully cross-platform Windows/Linux architecture, and resolving complex UI/IPC synchronization issues; additionally, the BOSS evaluation framework was integrated into the OpenPI LIBERO ecosystem. Meanwhile, through active code refactoring and benchmark adjustment strategies, the MIHD spatial transcriptomics analysis process was optimized. Cross-domain improvements also established a stable multi-round AI workflow mechanism, an effective caching management scheme, and a remote-interaction-based data synchronization model, thereby eliminating state crashes, context loss, and bandwidth bottlenecks in all active projects.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W12
item.description: This week focuses on building and validating high-computational-burden processes suitable for spatial omics, robot reinforcement learning, and conversational artificial intelligence systems. Key achievements include solving the challenges of error recovery benchmark tests through precise supervision alignment and loss reweighting, verifying the nonlinear spatial constraints of spatial transcriptomics via joint STAIG training, upgrading CalendarPro/Life Copilot with a hybrid semantic-word multi-intent architecture, as well as implementing enterprise-level cross-device synchronization and warehouse management that meet privacy requirements. System bottlenecks such as severe class imbalance, context overflow, process state differences, and database conflicts have been addressed without affecting the normal operation of core development processes.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W11
item.description: This week focused on large-scale architecture refactoring, stabilizing cross-framework dependencies, and the transformation of benchmark testing patterns in robot learning and spatial omics workflows. Key efforts included shifting “error recovery benchmarks” from traditional physical injection methods to a semantic architecture based on quota management; integrating scattered MIHD documents and spatial transcriptomics results; resolving the PyTorch/CUDA ABI mismatch issue that hinders VLA training efficiency. Additionally, the Research Scout/Profiler CLI was integrated with intelligent citation graph functionality, an MCP server for tool scheduling was deployed, and an adaptive GPU telemetry tool for Kubernetes namespace isolation was developed. Significant progress was made in process determinism, gradient scaling diagnostics, and cross-platform environment maintenance this week.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W10
item.description: This week, significant cross-domain optimization achievements were made. The efficiency of spatial transcriptome benchmarks and the robot VLA inference process was improved, while the macOS sandbox limitations were modernized, and the toolchain automation mechanism was unified. Key accomplishments include: separating the multimodal computation phase, reducing GPU overhead by over 85%; developing BatchedVLAServer, increasing accelerator utilization from approximately 10% to >60%; fixing the checkpoint normalization issue of scGPT, enhancing the ARI value by 44.4%; additionally, phases 1 to 3 of CalendarPro were completed, containing more than 360 stable test cases. Parallel work also integrated the AI documentation system, eliminated old symbolic link dependencies, and established a six-phase training framework, preparing for the upcoming promotion of the 8x A800 distributed framework.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W09
item.description: This week focuses on building and stabilizing a large-scale spatial transcriptomics integration pipeline and a robot evaluation framework, addressing key latent failures, hardware bottlenecks, and cross-framework alignment issues. Key milestones include restoring the integrity of the scGPT checkpoint, achieving 100-500 times acceleration in the pipeline through vectorization techniques, migrating BC-RNN to the official image pattern benchmark test, and establishing a reproducible multi-GPU LoRA training workflow. In terms of infrastructure, it involves HPC cluster configuration, secure GPU scheduling, and cross-device log aggregation, providing a solid foundation for long-term strategy training and domain-specific adaptive learning.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W08
item.description: This week, foundational MIHD spatial transcriptomics research was integrated, and the validation process for the second phase of error recovery benchmarks was also accelerated. By implementing self-supervised clustering engines (STEGO, BYOL+GAT, SCAN), using L2 normalization stable contrast loss, and reconstructing the visual encoder pipeline, key issues related to spatial coordinate extraction and basic model distribution changes were addressed. Parallel efforts successfully developed a two-phase AI daily reporting system with robust LLM output repair capabilities; the number of benchmark test scenarios increased to over 450, the BC-RNN baseline model was trained, and a dual-server VLA inference infrastructure was deployed. Infrastructure enhancements resolved issues such as SSH multiplexing conflicts, SLURM partition rejections, third-party pricing fluctuations, and HuggingFace compatibility problems, achieved through targeted fixed and dynamic resource allocation. Currently, focus is shifting toward relationship alignment validation, data expansion for MimicGen (over 500 examples), and optimizing the final M14/M6 multi-strategy evaluation process, preparing for paper writing.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W07
item.description: This week, comprehensive architectural and functional improvements were achieved in six core projects, including significant process optimization, stringent environmental safety enhancements, and scalable cross-platform tool support. The MIHD spatial omics workflow achieved a 62% reduction in redundant embedding computation through a two-stage extraction/caching architecture, while resolving the key HPC VRAM bottleneck and data integrity issues in the DLPFC region. The Error Recovery robot benchmark covered 118 different scenarios, successfully fixing issues such as MuJoCo force injection targets, OSC controller masking, and detector dead code infrastructure problems. Parallel work also enabled CalendarPro AI assistant to have batch operation capabilities, dual validation of intent parsing, and OAuth scope correction capabilities, while the Gadget/Summarize toolkit adopted an elastic two-stage multi-device architecture with atomic writing and centralized cloud synchronization via rclone. Related progress also extended the ccusage CLI pricing function to GLM models, standardized the Hugo static site generation process, and established strict repository documentation standards.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W06
item.description: This week’s focus is on stabilizing the MIHD multi-modal space fusion process, reverse engineering and integrating the QueST RM-Ideal evaluation framework, as well as building a secure automated reporting infrastructure. Key achievements include correcting errors in benchmark tests by implementing audit trails based on raw CSV files, aligning the end-to-end fusion architecture with the academic STAIG baseline, fixing the key masking logic in type matching metrics, and deploying a CI/CD process based on consensus mechanisms for external submissions. To ensure that space transcriptome benchmarks can be repeated on limited HPC clusters, emphasis was placed on environmental stability, infrastructure decoupling, and algorithm isolation.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W05
item.description: This week focused on stabilizing and aligning the MIHD spatial transcriptomics pipeline with the original STAIG framework. Critical benchmark accuracy regression was diagnosed and resolved by rectifying environment dependencies, restoring drifted hyperparameters, and correcting architectural discrepancies in graph convolution networks. A novel multimodal fusion configuration (GCN+UNI2) was successfully validated, establishing a robust baseline for future spatial multi-omics experiments.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2025-W40
item.description: The working week is characterized by the minimum level of activity, mainly including a initialization operation for the AutoSeg-SAM2 project. There is no substantial development, debugging, or task completion; the interactions are limited to context setting and placeholder messages. The focus is on ensuring file visibility, rather than making code-level modifications or solving technical challenges.
